# M3-12b: Anomaly alerts

- Milestone: M3
- Branch / worktree: `t/M3-12b`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M3-12b`
- Depends on: M3-12a
- Touches (exclusive while running): alerts/
- Plan refs: R11, §3.7, BACKLOG Plan questions 3
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (smoke: none; ships in M3-17)

## Goal
Deterministic rules flag duplicates, recurring price changes and unusually large charges, within the M3-12a budget.

## Scope
- Evaluate only transactions new since the last run, in Go, with no LLM.
- Duplicate: same payee + amount within 72h, different import ids.
- Recurring price change: same payee, more than 10% from the trailing median, needing at least 3 prior charges.
- Large: well above the same payee's history (builder picks a robust rule, needing at least 5 prior charges, and documents it in a comment).
- All are non-critical, deduped per transaction, sent through `Send`. Payee names are fine; no ids.
- Refunds, transfers and deleted rows are excluded.

## Out of scope
- Missing or short paycheck and tithing (M4, need `profile`). Actions on a duplicate.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Table tests per rule: fires, just under threshold, too little history.
- [ ] Test: a refund and a transfer never fire.
- [ ] Test: the same transaction doesn't alert twice across runs.
- [ ] Test: a burst of anomalies respects the budget.
- [ ] go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `alerts/anomalies.go`: `Alerter.Anomalies(ctx)` runs deterministic Go rules (no LLM) over rows from
    `TransactionsFirstSeenAfter(alert_cursor)`, sending each through `Send` (kinds `duplicate`, `price_change`,
    `large_charge`, all non-critical, dedupe key = transaction id; text names payee/account, never ids).
  - First run with no cursor is a silent baseline (cursor jumps to the newest row). The cursor is held before the first row
    whose Send failed (store error or Unsent post) so it retries; rows sharing a first_seen_at stand or fall together.
  - Exclusions: inflows (refunds), transfers, deleted rows, rows with no payee name. One alert per transaction across kinds
    (rule order duplicate → price change → large).
  - `alerts/alerts.go`: `Config.Mirror` (interface `Mirror`; `*store.DB` implements it). `alerts/anomalies_test.go`.
- Acceptance:
  - Table tests per rule (fires / just under / too little history): pass — `go test ./alerts -run 'TestAnomalies_(Duplicate|PriceChange|LargeCharge)'`
  - Refund and transfer (and deleted) never fire: pass — `TestAnomalies_RefundTransferDeletedNeverFire`
  - No alert twice across runs (incl. cursor rewind, a pair arriving together, cross-kind): pass —
    `TestAnomalies_NoAlertTwiceAcrossRuns`, `TestAnomalies_OneAlertPerTransactionAcrossKinds`, `TestAnomalies_FailedPostRetriesNextRun`
  - Burst respects budget (6 anomalies → 2 sent, 4 rolled_up): pass — `TestAnomalies_BurstRespectsBudget`
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`: pass. Threshold tests mutation-checked (flipping `<=`/`<` fails them).
- Deviations from brief:
  - Price change only fires for a *recurring* payee: its trailing (last ≤6) charges must sit within 2% of their median
    (all but one once the window has ≥5). Without this, every restaurant/grocery payee with ≥3 charges would fire on
    ordinary variance and burn the 2/month budget. Threshold is strictly more than 10%.
  - Duplicate requires both rows to carry import ids (brief: "different import ids"); dates within 3 days (YNAB dates
    have no time, so 72h = ≤3 days apart). A pair/cluster alerts once (skip if a partner already alerted duplicate).
  - Large rule (≥5 prior, last ≤24): amount > max(3×median, median + 6×1.4826×MAD, median + $25). Documented in code.
- Follow-ups for backlog: wire `Anomalies` into the scheduler after each successful sync with `Mirror: db` (M3-17 or
  whoever wires alerts); it is not called from `cmd` yet, like `Freshness`.
- Docs follow-ups: CLAUDE.md `alerts/` role (not yet listed): add the anomaly rules, the baseline on first run, and the
  recurring-bill qualifier for price change.
